mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a broad-based slowdown in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average combined with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals an overheating labor market, which triggers preemptive monetary tightening and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -2%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related sector earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) below their 12-month averages for three consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which reduces earnings across sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < 12-mo avg AND HOUST < 12-mo avg for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
